text:
marta: Heads-up — p99 on prod inference jumped from ~410ms to ~820ms after last night's deploy. Appears during steady traffic, not just spikes. Anyone else noticing tail blowups?

josh: Yea, I saw a couple hosts with repeated 700-900ms tails. p95 mostly ok ~200-300ms. Looks correlated with kernel routing change + batching tweak.

arun: Can you share profiler traces? Curious whether we fell back to the generic kernel for long sequences or if KV cache misses are spiking.

marta: Paste of the quick timeline + a log snippet:

[2026-03-16T23:02:11Z] scheduler: selected kernel=fused_gemm_fast for batch_id=4132 seq_avg=240 tokens
[2026-03-16T23:02:11Z] runtime: fallback kernel=generic_gemm for batch_id=4135 seq_avg=1890 tokens -> latency 812ms
[2026-03-16T23:02:12Z] kvcache: miss for req=... user=alpha -> warming kv page

perf-bot: profile summary (1h window): p50=118ms, p95=340ms, p99=820ms; kv_hit_rate dropped 72% -> 59% after deploy; kv_evictions 18k/hr -> 62k/hr.

chris: That kv_hit_rate drop is huge. If continuous batching is merging requests across users, KV thrash could explain fallback to long-seq paths (more tokens, different kernel choice).

tao: Also check scheduler "batch shaping" — if microbursts are forming very large max_token batches, the kernel selector might choose fallback kernels optimized for long sequences but slower.

arun: Possible knobs to test: reduce max_batch_tokens to avoid giant microbatches, or increase queue_window_ms so we smooth bursts and improve KV reuse. Also reorder fallback kernels so fused_gemm remains first for mid-length sequences.

marta: Current scheduler config from prod (post-deploy):

```
scheduler:
  queue_window_ms: 6
  max_wait_ms: 12
  max_batch_tokens: 8192
kernel_routing:
  preferred: [fused_gemm_fast, fast_attn_qkv]
  fallback: [generic_gemm]
```

josh: My hypothesis: short queue_window (6ms) forces more eager batching which sometimes combines heterogeneous requests -> bigger avg seq length per batch -> kernel fallback + kv misses.

chris: Two quick experiments: 1) lower max_batch_tokens -> 4096 2) increase queue_window_ms -> 14ms (give more time to coalesce similar seq lengths). Try them independently.

marta: I'll spin a canary with max_batch_tokens=4096 on canary-2 group and collect p95/p99 + kv_hit for 30m.

deploy-bot: rollout started: canary-2 (8 hosts) -> applying scheduler.max_batch_tokens=4096.

perf-bot: canary baseline (pre-change): p95=360ms p99=790ms kv_hit=61%

[30m later]

perf-bot: canary results: p95=345ms p99=610ms kv_hit=64% (kv_evictions down 35%). CPU diff negligible.

josh: Nice — p99 improvement and better kv_hit suggests smaller max_batch avoided mixing requests that evicted KV entries.

marta: Next test: queue_window_ms=14 on a separate canary group to check smoothing effect.

deploy-bot: rollout started: canary-3 (6 hosts) -> applying scheduler.queue_window_ms=14.

perf-bot: canary-3 baseline (pre-change): p95=352ms p99=780ms kv_hit=62%

[30m later]

perf-bot: canary-3 results: p95=330ms p99=420ms kv_hit=70% (tail massively improved). Throughput slightly better due to fewer fallback kernels.

arun: So two takeaways: lowering max_batch_tokens reduced KV thrash; increasing queue_window smoothed sequence heterogeneity and kept fast kernels active.

chris: For rollback risk, we should also pin kernel fallback ordering and add a guard in kernel selector: if KV miss rate > 50% prefer kernels that are robust to misses (or reduce batch size dynamically).

marta: Agreed. Plan: revert prod to (A) max_batch_tokens=4096 and (B) queue_window_ms=12, monitor 2h. Also add selector guard and an alert if p99>600ms or kv_hit drops >5% from baseline.

tao: I'll draft an SRE runbook entry: how to flip these knobs and how to read perf-bot outputs for KV/percentiles.

marta: Thanks all. Leaving the canary on canary-2/3 until 02:00 UTC, then promote if stable. Filing a follow-up to tune kernel routing weights and add an offline microbenchmark to predict kernel fallback for mixed-batch seq distributions. :thumbsup:

josh: +1

perf-bot: note: scheduled job 'kv-warmup' set to run hourly to reduce cold miss bursts.

marta: closing loop later with numbers. If anyone sees sudden p99 spike ping here.
